build: original disk, Rapidlok V6, PAL, C64 Preservation Project gunship_s1/s2[microprose_1985](rl6)(pal)

comments.text: Line 0: REM, five DEL characters and a shifted L. LIST prints a REM's bytes as they are, so the DELs rub out the "0 REM" it has just printed, and the shifted L, a byte with no keyword, stops LIST with ?SYNTAX ERROR before the next line. Every BASIC program in the game starts so.

Line 1 switches off RESTORE (NMI vector to an RTI) and the CIA's interrupts, lowers BASIC's top to $1300 and clears the variables. Line 2 sets the constants (19000), builds the mission's tables (900), loads the flight's files (14000), then lines 3-5 print LOAD "g2",8,1 on the screen, put a RETURN in the keyboard buffer and end with NEW, so BASIC loads G2 itself.
Lines 10-11: copies L pages from page F to page T through all of RAM (move_ram), F, T and L being page numbers that may carry a fraction for an offset inside the page.

Lines 900-949: the mission's tables for the flight. MP$ becomes the theatre's two letters (tn, se, ca, me, we) from $035E, the theatre number the front end left in the cassette buffer. Sixty-four values from DATA go to $5398-$53D7. The two mission targets' twelve-byte records are copied from the theatre file's table at $9000 (index from $035C and $035D) to $53E0 and $53EC, and one more value from $909C to $53FB.
Lines 940-949: picks one of the twelve rows of ten values below, by theatre and enemy level (theatre*3 + $0340 - 3), and copies it to $53A9-$53B2, over the defaults line 910 put there.
Lines 960-977: twelve rows of ten values, one row for each theatre from Southeast Asia to Western Europe and each of its three enemy levels. Training keeps the defaults of lines 920-923.
Lines 9000-9002: loads the file named F$ with the KERNAL's LOAD, through call (SETLFS and SETNAM at 19520), and tries again until the status says it worked.

Lines 14000-14095: first copies eight pages from $A800 to $C800, then loads the flight's files in turn and moves each piece where the flight wants it. cp, then its pieces to $4000, $D040, $F040, $7C00, $EE08 and $6000; ch, then its pieces to $E300, $5100 (half a page more at night) and $E200; the theatre's terrain w3.<theatre> (Western Europe's for training), with a page to $1A86; m, the engine; and m.<theatre><n>, n being 4 minus the enemy level, which line 14095 loads last.
Lines 19000-19004: FNLB(X) gives the low byte of X as the copy routines take it, the helpers' addresses (SB, MV, BM, KE, S6, M6), A0-A6 = 165-171 ($A5-$AB, the helpers' registers), KP = 256.
Lines 19520-19528: puts the file name in memory at 1006 ($03EE), then calls the KERNAL's SETLFS (device 8, secondary address 1) and SETNAM through call.
